thread.title: The Nasdaq Came This Close to a Bear Market Thursday

title: The Nasdaq Came This Close to a Bear Market Thursday
text:
The Nasdaq Came This Close to a Bear Market Thursday By Dec. 20, 2018 4:33 p.m. ET Order Reprints Illustration by Michael Haddad Text size
4:10 p.m. One day after the Fed freaked out investors , the Nasdaq Composite ended Thursday half a percentage point away from the 20% threshold that would officially quality the drop as a bear market.
The Nasdaq fell 1.6% to 6,528.41 today, off 19.50% from its all-time closing high. The S&P 500 dropped 1.6% to 267.42—down 15.81% from its high—while the Dow Jones Industrial Average slumped 464.06 points, or 2%, to 22,859.60, and is now 14.79% off its high.
The Nasdaq briefly entered a bear market during the day, and It probably shouldn’t come as a surprise that it is the first of the major indexes to experience a near miss. Its biggest stocks — Apple (AAPL), Amazon.com (AMZN), and Facebook (FB) among them—were the ones that led the market higher. Now, all three are in bear markets of their own: Apple closed down 33% from its 52-week high, while Facebook is 39% off its high, and Amazon has dropped 29% from its own 52-week high.
The pain in once-highflying stocks should give investors pause, writes Jonathan Krinsky , chief market technician at Bay Crest Partners . He writes that stocks like Amazon, Adobe (ADBE), Autodesk (ADSK), Boeing (BA), Domino’s Pizza (DPZ), Alphabet (GOOGL), Microsoft (MSFT), and Visa (V)--which had been among the markets best performers this year—are only now starting to drop. “The biggest issue, in our view, is we are just now starting to see some of the prior leaders of the bull market breakdown from major tops,” he explains. “We expect those need to see breakdowns and washouts before a longer-lasting bottom.” Among those stocks, only Alphabet is down on the year, and only by 2.8%.
But look at the bright side—at least the Nasdaq managed to avoid a bear market today. Tomorrow’s another question.
